outcome: No result found since 26 January 2024 that changes what a careful person would write in this bullet: the general conjecture that Ax^m - By^n = C has finitely many solutions (for (m,n) not both 2) remains open, with only pre-existing partial results and post-window papers on related-but-distinct equations found.
summary: I searched extensively for any post-26-January-2024 progress on the specific conjecture stated in the bullet — that for fixed A, B, C the equation Ax^m - By^n = C has finitely many solutions in x, y, m, n when (m,n) are not both 2 — and found none. I examined the Wikipedia article (unchanged in substance, still lists only pre-2011 references and no update reflecting new progress) and several arXiv papers that surfaced in searches: (1) Miyazaki & Pink, 'Number of solutions to a special type of unit equations in two unknowns, III' (arXiv:2403.20037, submitted 29 March 2024, revised 12 April 2025) — this studies a^x + b^y = c^z (a Jesmanowicz/Terai-type unit equation) and Bennett's related conjecture on a^x - b^y = c for fixed small c, citing Pillai-type equations only as background/motivation, not proving anything about the general A,B,C-parameterized conjecture; (2) Styer, arXiv:2402.04428 (Feb 2024) and (3) arXiv:2407.07407 (July 2024) — both study the same a^x + b^y = c^z equation, a three-term generalization distinct from the bullet's two-term Ax^m - By^n = C equation, and only cite Pillai's equation a^x - b^y = c as related prior work. None of these papers restrict or specialize the conjecture as literally stated (fixed general A, B, C); they address a different equation with an extra term and different variable structure, which is a related problem under §3.1's test, not a case of this one. I found no AI involvement anywhere in this space. The status is 'open' with no_change_found true, matching and confirming the triage's 'none' verdict.
competing_reading: One could argue the Miyazaki-Pink 2403.20037 result on a^x - b^y = c for c = 13 (a special case of the two-term Pillai equation with fixed C=13, A=B=1) is a 'case' of the stated conjecture rather than a 'related problem', since it does specialize A=1, B=1 and fixes C. However, this specific sub-case (A=B=1) was already resolved by earlier work (Bennett's 2001 result gives at most two solutions for any fixed f in x^n - y^m = f), so even under this reading the 2024/2025 paper is refining/extending an already-settled special case (via the three-term equation, using it as a tool) rather than advancing the general A,B,C conjecture itself — it does not change this bullet's entry either way.
what_would_settle_it: A paper proving a finiteness or non-finiteness result for the equation Ax^m - By^n = C for general or newly-unbounded ranges of A, B, C (not just A=B=1 or a single fixed C), or an explicit statement in a survey/expert digestion (e.g., an update to Waldschmidt's 'Perfect Powers' survey or the Bennett 'Pillai's conjecture revisited' line of work) that the general conjecture status changed after January 2024.
